reference_title: Standard Practice Manual for Flexible Pavements

figures.caption: Batch Plant (Courtesy of National Asphalt Pavement Association (NAPA))
figures.description: Schematic of a batch-type hot-mix asphalt plant: cold-feed bins, dryer, hot elevator, screens/hot bins, weigh box, and pugmill mixer (Section 2-2.1.1).

figures.caption: Drum Mix Plant (Courtesy of NAPA)
figures.description: Schematic of a drum-mix (parallel/counter-flow) hot-mix asphalt plant, where drying and mixing occur continuously in the same drum (Section 2-2.1.2).

figures.caption: Minimum Anticipated Pavement Temperature as a Function of DFI
figures.description: Chart relating the design air-freezing index (DFI) to the minimum anticipated pavement temperature, used to select the low-temperature PG binder grade in cold regions (Section 2-3.1.4.3; see also table_2_5_asphalt_grade_by_freezing_index).

figures.caption: Gradation Curves for Stockpile Samples
figures.description: Example semi-log gradation curves (percent passing vs. sieve size) for individual aggregate stockpile samples, used when proportioning cold-feed aggregates for HMA (Section 2-4.2).

figures.caption: Gradation Curves for Bin Samples
figures.description: Example gradation curves for hot-bin samples taken after the plant's screening/bin-splitting process, compared against the stockpile gradations of Figure 2-4.

figures.caption: VTM vs. Asphalt Content
figures.description: One of six sub-plots in Figure 2-6(a-f), 'Asphalt Paving Mix Design for Typical Mix' (Section 2-4.2.6/2-4.2.7): voids in total mix (VTM) plotted against asphalt cement content, decreasing as asphalt content increases.

figures.caption: Unit Weight vs. Asphalt Content
figures.description: One of six sub-plots in Figure 2-6(a-f): total mix unit weight plotted against asphalt cement content, peaking at a slightly higher asphalt content than the stability curve (Figure 2-6e).

figures.caption: VMA vs. Asphalt Content
figures.description: One of six sub-plots in Figure 2-6(a-f): voids in mineral aggregate (VMA) plotted against asphalt cement content, forming a characteristic U-shaped curve as asphalt lubricates then pushes apart aggregate particles.

figures.caption: Voids Filled vs. Asphalt Content
figures.description: One of six sub-plots in Figure 2-6(a-f): percent voids filled with asphalt (VFA) plotted against asphalt cement content, increasing toward a maximum in the same manner VTM approaches a minimum.

figures.caption: Stability vs. Asphalt Content
figures.description: One of six sub-plots in Figure 2-6(a-f): Marshall stability plotted against asphalt cement content, increasing to a peak then decreasing (not used for Superpave mix design).

figures.caption: Flow vs. Asphalt Content
figures.description: One of six sub-plots in Figure 2-6(a-f): Marshall flow plotted against asphalt cement content, increasing at an increasing rate (not used for Superpave mix design).

figures.caption: Mat Density Control Chart
figures.description: Example quality-control chart plotting individual and 4-sample moving-average mat density results against the acceptable density band, used to detect an out-of-control compaction process (Section 2-4.4).

figures.caption: Types of HMA Deficiencies and Probable Causes
figures.description: Diagnostic chart linking observed HMA mixture/construction deficiencies to their probable causes, for troubleshooting during production and placement (Section 2-4.4).

figures.caption: Types of HMA Pavement Imperfections and Probable Causes
figures.description: Diagnostic chart linking observed finished-pavement surface imperfections to their probable causes (faulty laying/rolling, mix design, or plant operation) (Section 2-4.4.6).

figures.caption: Classification of Mix Systems by Cohesion Test Curves
figures.description: Cohesiometer test curve classification chart used in micro-surfacing mix design to characterize a mixture's set/cure behavior (Section 4-5.3.1).

figures.caption: Mineral Filler Content Optimization "Benedict Curve"
figures.description: The 'Benedict Curve' relating micro-surfacing mineral filler content to mixture consistency/working time, used to select the optimum filler dosage (Section 4-5.3.1).

figures.caption: Determination of Optimum Asphalt Content
figures.description: Chart used to determine the optimum asphalt (emulsion residue) content for micro-surfacing mixtures from wet-track abrasion and other design test results (Section 4-5.3.2).
